evidence.claim: Model risk score 0.76. In the 0.70-0.85 band the bank's closed history holds 817 confirmed frauds against 234 cleared alarms, a likelihood ratio of 0.67 - mildly exculpatory, consistent with the dataset note that above 0.70 most flagged transactions turn out to be legitimate

The identity record marks this device New for the account. 83% of cleared alarms had a New device against 18% of confirmed fraud: on its own a new device is the signature of a cardholder who has just bought a phone, not of a compromise
A online transaction on a card whose history is 1% online. Measured on the closed cases this is mildly exculpatory (11.9% of cleared vs 4.5% of confirmed fraud)
25 transactions on this card in the 48 hours ending at the flagged one. A burst of ten or more is 1.9x more likely on confirmed fraud
The bank has 3 confirmed-fraud case(s) already closed on this card (CC-4294, CC-3216, CC-1475), pattern(s): account_takeover, card_not_present_new_device

External email-domain intelligence classifies 'gmail.com' as a free webmail address, which is what most real cardholders and most fraudsters both use. Measured across the bank's closed cases this is the baseline -- it appears on 3,667 confirmed frauds and 573 cleared alarms -- so it is named as context and carries no weight.

The 5 closed cases whose transaction most resembles this one (CC-0904, CC-2287, CC-4735, CC-1898, CC-0796) closed as 2 confirmed fraud (card not present new device) and 3 cleared. Cited as memory; it carries no weight, because it resembles on the same features the score already uses

Connected components place this card in the graph's giant device-sharing component (2,500 cards). Transitive device sharing percolates at every threshold tested, so membership is not evidence of a ring and carries no weight here; it is recorded because policy R6 asks for the shared element to be named.

Known fraud pattern 5: Account takeover: Account takeover. Mixed-channel activity inconsistent with the cardholder, often with device and match-flag anomalies, pointing to stolen credentials rather than a stolen number.

Policy rule R1: Verify before you block on a weak signal: R1. Verify before you block on a weak signal. If the case rests on a single signal (including a risk score alone) and your assessed fraud probability is below 0.70, recommend `VERIFY_WITH_CUSTOMER` or `STEP_UP_AUTH` before any block. Blocking a legitimate customer on one signal is a policy breach.

case.summary: Risk score on card C07671-K2 over a $35.66 online transaction on 2016-12-09. Against it: The bank has 3 confirmed-fraud case(s) already closed on this card (CC-4294, CC-3216, CC-1475), pattern(s): account_takeover, card_not_present_new_device. 25 transactions on this card in the 48 hours ending at the flagged one. For the cardholder: The identity record marks this device New for the account. Step-up authentication passed. Assessed as legitimate at fraud probability 0.28; no transaction is treated as part of a fraud episode and exposure is zero.

evidence_requests.reason: R1: probability 0.41 is below 0.70; ask the cardholder before taking any action with customer impact.
evidence_requests.assumed_response: No reply within 24 hours. ASSUMPTION: no replies ship with this dataset, and nothing independent in the evidence points to what the cardholder would say. Inventing an answer here would manufacture certainty, so the agent assumes the case policy R4 is written for - the customer does not respond - and acts accordingly.

evidence_requests.reason: Policy 5: the cardholder did not answer the verification request, and step-up authentication is the other channel the agent may use without approval.
evidence_requests.assumed_response: One-time passcode completed successfully from the cardholder's registered number. ASSUMPTION: simulated; no authentication responses ship with the dataset. Derived from the card-detail match flags (a mismatch fails it), not from the agent's own probability.

next_best_actions.what_changed: No reply within 24 hours, moving assessed probability to 0.28. Added: ALLOW_TRANSACTION, CLOSE_NO_FRAUD. Dropped: CREATE_CASE, ESCALATE_TO_ANALYST, VERIFY_WITH_CUSTOMER.

sar.reason: Policy 3a: a report requires fraud confirmed or strongly suspected. Assessed probability 0.28 with verdict 'legitimate' does not meet that bar.

stop_reason: Policy 6: probability 0.28 on 6 independent pieces of evidence sits between the stopping thresholds, and every request the agent may make without approval has been made. The remaining uncertainty is the cardholder's own intent, which only the cardholder or an analyst can resolve; the recommended actions route it to them rather than resolving it in the graph.
